# How the Sleep Cycle App Works

**Sleep Cycle** is a popular sleep tracking and smart alarm app available on both iOS and Android. Here's a breakdown of how it works:

## 🎤 Sleep Tracking (No Wearable Needed)
Sleep Cycle uses your **phone's microphone** (its patented sound technology) or **accelerometer** to monitor your sleep throughout the night — no smartwatch or wearable required. You simply place your phone on your nightstand or nearby.

- The **microphone** picks up sounds like breathing patterns, movement, snoring, coughing, and sleep talking.
- The **accelerometer** (if you place the phone on your mattress) detects body movements.
- These signals are mapped to **sleep stages** (light sleep, deep sleep, REM, and awake periods), giving you a detailed sleep graph in the morning.

## ⏰ Smart Alarm
This is the app's signature feature. Instead of waking you at a fixed time, it wakes you during your **lightest sleep phase** within a **30-minute window** you set. For example, if your alarm is set for 7:00 AM, the app will find the best moment between 6:30–7:00 AM when you're in light sleep. Waking from light sleep means **less grogginess** (sleep inertia) compared to being jolted out of deep sleep.

## 📊 Sleep Analysis & Reports
Each morning you get:
- Total sleep duration
- Time spent in each sleep stage
- Number of times you woke up
- A "sleep quality" percentage
- Trends over time (weekly, monthly)

## 🔊 Sound Recording
The app can record sounds during the night, so you can listen back and discover if you **snore**, talk in your sleep, or are disturbed by external noises.

## 🌙 Sleep Aids
Sleep Cycle offers **sleep stories, ambient sounds, and relaxation content** with a soft fade-out to help you fall asleep.

## 🤖 AI Sleep Coach (Luma)
The app includes an AI-powered sleep coach called **Luma** that provides personalized guidance and tips based on your sleep patterns.

## ⚠️ Things to Keep in Mind
- **It's not medical-grade** — sleep stage estimates come from phone sensors, not clinical equipment (like a polysomnography in a sleep lab).
- **Background noise can affect accuracy** — ambient sounds (fans, traffic, a partner) may distort microphone-based analysis.
- **Free vs. Premium** — the core smart alarm and basic tracking are free; premium adds snore detection, detailed analysis, and the full sleep aid library.

Overall, it's a convenient, non-invasive way to get insights into your sleep habits and wake up feeling more refreshed!

## What Sleep Cycle Can Do for CPAP Users
- Sleep Cycle is a **general sleep tracker and smart alarm** that monitors your sleep stages (light, deep, REM) using your phone's microphone or accelerometer.
- It can **indirectly** help you see if CPAP therapy is improving your sleep quality — by comparing your sleep graphs on nights with and without CPAP, you may notice differences in sleep disturbances and overall sleep quality.
- Sleep Cycle is also developing an **AI-powered sleep apnea screening tool**, currently in clinical trials in Australia, but this is a screening feature — not a CPAP data integration.

If you want to track your actual CPAP data (AHI, mask seal, usage hours, pressure, etc.), dedicated CPAP apps are the way to go:

| **CPAP Tracker & Journal** | Manual logging of pressure, humidity, symptoms; exportable CSV for your doctor |
| **OSCAR** (desktop) | Free, open-source desktop software for detailed CPAP data analysis |

Many CPAP users **run Sleep Cycle alongside their CPAP app** — Sleep Cycle for general sleep quality/staging insights and smart alarm, and a CPAP-specific app for therapy compliance data. This gives you the most complete picture to share with your sleep doctor.

# Sleep Tracker App UI — Design Principles & Inspiration

Here's an overview of what makes a great sleep tracker app UI, based on current design trends and top-rated apps:

---

## 🎨 Color & Theme

- **Dark mode is king.** Nearly every well-regarded sleep tracker uses a dark background by default. Users often check these apps at bedtime or upon waking — a bright white screen is jarring. Dark palettes reduce eye strain at night.
- **Calm, nocturnal accent colors.** Deep blues, purples, and teals are the go-to accent palette — colors associated with night and dreams. Bright pops of color (cyan, violet, soft orange) are used sparingly to highlight key data points.
- **Light/dark variants.** Top apps like Sleep Cycle offer both a pure white daytime mode and a dark nighttime mode to suit user preferences.

## 📊 Data Visualization (The Core of the UI)

- **Graph-first layout.** The centerpiece of most sleep tracker UIs is a **sleep stage graph** — showing awake, light, deep, and REM sleep across the night. This is the first thing users see on their dashboard.
- **Trend lines & weekly/monthly views.** Beyond single-night data, the best UIs show sleep quality trends over time with simple line or bar charts.
- **Sleep score / quality ring.** A prominent circular or numerical "sleep score" (e.g., 85/100) gives users an at-a-glance summary without needing to interpret raw data.

## 🧭 Layout & Navigation

- **Clear hierarchy.** Large, bold headings for the sleep score or hours slept, with secondary text for details like bedtime, wake time, and interruptions.
- **Minimal, uncluttered screens.** The best designs resist cramming every metric onto one screen. Key info is front and center; deeper analytics are one tap away.
- **Large touch targets.** Buttons and interactive elements are sized generously — users are often groggy when interacting with these apps.

## 🏆 Top Apps Known for Great UI

| App | UI Highlight |
|-----|-------------|
| **Sleep Cycle** | Clean smart-alarm interface, gentle wake-up curve graph |
| **Pillow** | Deep Apple ecosystem integration, beautiful Apple Watch complications |
| **Oura Ring** | Polished readiness/sleep score dashboard with rich data layers |
| **Samsung Health** | Free, no-subscription sleep tracking with a clear summary card |
| **SleepScore** | Phone-only (no wearable needed), science-backed visualizations |

## ✨ Key Design Trends (2025–2026)

1. **Onboarding that educates** — Brief, illustrated walkthroughs explaining what each metric means
2. **Actionable insights over raw data** — "You slept 40 min less than your goal" instead of just numbers
3. **Haptic & sound design** — Smart alarm UIs that visualize the gentle wake-up window
4. **Widget-first design** — Lock screen and home screen widgets showing last night's score at a glance
5. **AI-powered recommendations** — Personalized bedtime suggestions surfaced in a conversational UI card

# Using Sleep Cycle with a Partner

If you and your partner both sleep in the same bed and use the Sleep Cycle app, here's what you need to know:

---

## 🔗 Partner Linking Feature (iPhone Only)

Sleep Cycle has a **Partner Linking** feature that connects two iPhones so the app can distinguish between you and your partner's movements/sounds during sleep.

**How to set it up:**
1. Both you and your partner need Sleep Cycle installed on your iPhones.
2. Both phones must be connected to the **same Wi-Fi network**.
3. Go to **Profile → More → Partner Linking** on each device.
4. The two phones will detect each other and link up.

**Key details:**
- A **link symbol** will appear on your night screen when the devices are connected.
- Your sleep data **remains private** — it's not shared between devices. The link is only used to improve tracking accuracy.
- If you're not in the same room, the link won't affect your data.

---

## ⚠️ Limitations

- **Android:** Partner Linking is **not available** on Android yet.
- **Microphone mode required:** The feature works when both phones use the **microphone** as the motion/sound detector (not the accelerometer).

## 💡 Tips for Sleeping with a Partner (Without Linking)

- Sleep Cycle says the app **works well even without linking**, though accuracy may improve with it.
- You can label your partner's sounds as "other" to filter them out.

# How to Edit Your Wake-Up Time in the Sleep Cycle App

Here's how to change your wake-up alarm time in the **Sleep Cycle** app:

## On the Main Screen (Alarm Clock)
1. **Open the Sleep Cycle app.**
2. On the main/home screen, you'll see your current **alarm time** displayed prominently.
3. **Tap the alarm time** — this will open a time picker (scroll wheel or dial).
4. **Scroll or adjust** to your desired wake-up time.
5. Confirm your selection.

## Adjust the Wake-Up Window
Sleep Cycle doesn't just ring at a fixed time — it uses a **wake-up phase** (window) to wake you during light sleep *before* your set time. To adjust this:

1. Go to **Profile** (or **Settings** ⚙️).
2. Look for **"Wake-up phase"** or **"Alarm window."**
3. Choose a window length (e.g., **30 minutes** is the default). This means if your alarm is set for 7:00 AM, the app may wake you anytime between 6:30–7:00 AM when it detects light sleep.

## Set Different Times for Different Days (Sleep Goal)
1. Go to **Profile** → **Sleep Goal**.
2. You can set separate wake-up and bedtime targets for **weekdays vs. weekends** (or all days).

> **Tip:** If you find the alarm always goes off at the very end of your window, try widening the wake-up phase so the app has a better chance of catching a light-sleep moment.
